blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Tool-use benchmarks often score agents by final task success, but terminal outcomes can obscure whether the intermediate tool-call trajectory was executable. We propose prefix executability as a trajectory-level evaluation protocol for tool-using agents. The protocol measures whether every prefix of a predicted tool-call sequence remains executable under tool schemas, state preconditions, and data dependencies, and summarizes reliability using Prefix Executability Curves (PEC), First-Error Depth (FED), Trajectory Executability Rate (TER), horizon-normalized AUC-PEC, and Recovery Rate (RR). We instantiate the protocol on stratified samples from BFCL-v3 multi-turn and ToolSandbox, and on the complete Airline/Retail base splits of $τ^3$-bench. We observe that outcome-only and prefix-level rankings diverge: agents whose execution is conditioned on an unverified plan often achieve higher point-estimate final success than non-plan-conditioned baselines while substantially lowering TER and AUC-PEC. These divergences are precisely the failure modes that prefix executability is designed to expose: they reveal whether apparent success rests on an executable trajectory, where invalidity first enters, and whether success follows recovery from an earlier failure. As a validation intervention, explicit pre-execution plan checking can improve executable-prefix survival while maintaining competitive terminal success. These results show that final success alone is insufficient for evaluating tool-use agents and that prefix-level executability provides an actionable reliability signal for comparing agents, diagnosing failures, and assessing validation mechanisms.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Tool-using language agents operate over APIs, user-defined tools, and interactive software environments where correctness depends on more than a final answer. A valid run must maintain an executable sequence of intermediate actions while respecting tool schemas, cross-step dependencies, and evolving environment state [ 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 ] . This requirement is especially acute in multi-turn settings, where an early invalid call can corrupt later state or force the agent into recovery behavior that is invisible to outcome-only scoring [ 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 ] . Consider a service workflow in which an agent first retrieves a record, then passes the returned identifier to update, payment, or notification tools. A later call may be syntactically well formed but non-executable if it references a stale identifier, skips a required precondition, or applies an update before the corresponding state exists; a subsequent repair can still produce the desired final state while hiding where the trajectory first became invalid.
blocks.zh: 工具使用语言代理在API,用户自定义的工具,以及交互软件环境中运行,其正确性取决于不止一个最终答案. 有效的运行必须保持一个可执行的中间动作序列,同时尊重工具计划、跨步骤依赖性以及不断变化的环境状态[1、2、3、4]。 这一要求在多回合设置中特别尖锐,早期无效的呼叫可能腐蚀后期状态或迫使代理进入只见结果分数[3,4,5,6]的恢复行为. 考虑一个服务工作流程,其中代理人首先检索记录,然后通过返回的标识符更新、支付或通知工具。 后继调用如果引用了 Stale 标识符,跳过一个必要的先决条件,或者在相应状态存在之前应用更新,则可能在战术上形成好的但不可执行;后续的修复仍然可以产生所期望的最终状态,同时隐藏轨道最初变得无效的地方.

blocks.en: Recent evaluation work has moved beyond simple terminal accuracy. T-Eval decomposes tool use into step-wise subskills [ 7 ] ; ToolSandbox evaluates task-specified intermediate and final conditions and checks for prohibited states or events [ 4 ] ; TRAJECT-Bench scores tool selection, argument correctness, and dependency ordering over full trajectories [ 8 ] ; ToolPRMBench and AgentProcessBench assess local process quality [ 9 , 10 ] ; and procedure-aware evaluation shows that nominally successful runs can still violate task procedures [ 11 ] . TRACE adds reference-free assessment of efficiency, hallucination, and adaptivity over tool-use trajectories [ 12 ] . Robustness studies further probe query perturbations, tool-set changes, and injected execution faults [ 13 , 14 ] . These efforts make a remaining gap clear: standard metrics still rarely quantify how long a naturally generated rollout remains executable before its first invalid prefix, or how often final success is achieved only after entering a failure regime.
blocks.zh: 最近进行的评价工作已经超越了简单的终端准确性。 T-Eval将工具分解为分步操作的子技能[7]; ToolSandbox评价指定任务的中间和最终条件以及对被禁状态或事件的检查[4];TRAJECT-Bench的分数工具选择,论证正确性,以及完整轨迹的依赖性命令[8];TolPRMBench和AgentProcess Bench评估本地的流程质量[9,10];以及程序认识评价显示名义上成功的运行仍然可能违反任务程序[11]. TRACE在工具使用轨迹上增加了效率、幻觉和可适性无参考评估[12]。 强力研究进一步探查查询扰动,工具集变化,并注入执行断层 [13,14]. 这些努力明确了尚存的差距:标准衡量标准仍然很少量化在第一个无效前缀之前自然产生的推出仍可执行的时间,或者在进入失败制度后最终成功的次数。

blocks.en: Prefix executability complements these evaluations by checking the execution feasibility of the actual emitted rollout under explicit tool and state semantics. It credits alternative executable action sequences without requiring one gold path and records first failure, survival, and recovery. Appendix A compares what prior evaluation protocols measure.

We study prefix-level executability failures : trajectory prefixes that may look plausible as text but are non-executable under the available tool schema, explicit preconditions, cross-step references, or current environment state. We argue that prefix executability is a missing reliability axis because final success and reference-trajectory match conflate three questions: how long the rollout remains valid, where validity first breaks, and whether later actions recover from the break. We therefore formalize executable prefixes and report a metric family centered on Prefix Executability Curves (PEC), First-Error Depth (FED), horizon-normalized AUC-PEC, Trajectory Executability Rate (TER), and Recovery Rate (RR). These metrics primarily diagnose reliability; when reported alongside trajectory
length, latency, or monetary cost, they also support efficiency-sensitive
analysis by distinguishing short, valid rollouts from long or failure-prone ones.

blocks.en: These distinctions are operationally important in cost-sensitive tool use. In workflows that trigger external transactions, consume scarce resources, modify persistent state, or require human escalation, the depth of the first invalid action can determine both the cost of failure and the feasibility of recovery. Prefix executability therefore provides a practical evaluation signal for deciding not only whether an agent eventually succeeds, but also whether execution remains uninterrupted or requires recovery along the way.
blocks.zh: 在使用成本敏感的工具方面,这些区别在业务上很重要。 在触发外部交易,消耗稀缺资源,改变持续状态,或需要人力升级的工作流程中,第一个无效行动的深度可以决定失败的代价和回收的可行性. 因此,前缀可执行性提供了一个实用的评价信号,不仅用于决定代理人最终是否成功,而且用于判断执行是否不间断地进行,或者需要沿途收回.

blocks.en: The paper is evaluation-first. We deliberately use a minimal Dual-Loop planner-verifier intervention only as a controlled probe: we test whether pre-execution validation improves those metrics even when final success rankings tell a different story. This framing separates the evaluation contribution from the particular intervention and lets us ask when plan conditioning helps tool use, and when it amplifies invalid intermediate structure.

blocks.en: Our contributions are: 1. We formalize executable prefixes for tool-using agents and define PEC, FED, TER, AUC-PEC, and RR as a prefix-level evaluation protocol for variable-horizon trajectories. Appendix B establishes exact properties and consistency under explicit sampling assumptions. 2. We instantiate the protocol on BFCL v3 multi-turn and ToolSandbox with stratified 200-example samples, and on all 164 Airline/Retail base-split tasks in τ 3 \tau^{3} -bench, using shared task IDs across methods and models, and task-level confidence intervals. 3. We show that outcome-only and prefix-level rankings can diverge: unverified plan conditioning can improve final success while sharply reducing executability, whereas pre-execution validation consistently improves TER, AUC-PEC, and early PEC across three LLM conditions on BFCL v3 and ToolSandbox. A representative BFCL setting illustrates the pattern: an unverified plan-conditioned executor can reach the correct terminal outcome while emitting invalid intermediate tool-call prefixes, whereas Dual-Loop preserves terminal performance while restoring prefix executability. The τ 3 \tau^{3} -bench audit further demonstrates that prefix reliability and terminal success can rank methods differently.

blocks.en: Table 1 summarizes the evaluation signals used in our study and how the proposed prefix-level metrics complement standard outcome and reference-match scores. Exact-call and trajectory-match metrics measure agreement with a reference solution, but they do not localize the first invalid prefix and may penalize alternative executable trajectories. Final success captures task utility, but does not indicate whether the rollout remained executable throughout or succeeded only after an earlier invalid action. PEC, FED, TER, AUC-PEC, and RR fill this gap by measuring prefix survival, first-error depth, full-trajectory executability, normalized executable-prefix area, and recovery after prefix failure.

blocks.en: 2.5 Validation Intervention
blocks.zh: 2.5 验证干预

blocks.en: Dual-Loop is included as a controlled validation intervention, not as the main architectural claim. Given the user goal, tool schema, and a compact state summary, a planner proposes a structured plan. A verifier checks tool existence, schema conformity, explicit preconditions, and variable bindings. If verification fails, the planner revises the plan using verifier feedback; once verification succeeds, the approved plan conditions a ReAct executor, which alone issues environment tool calls. Planner and verifier messages are therefore method-side computation, not benchmark tool actions, and all prefix metrics are computed on the executed tool trajectory. The intervention follows planner-executor and verifier-guided generation work, but here serves as a stress test for the evaluation protocol [ 18 , 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 ] . Appendix D gives the schematic.

blocks.en: We use BFCL v3 and ToolSandbox to test multi-step function-calling correctness and stateful on-policy interaction. BFCL v3 provides multi-turn function-calling scenarios under a standardized interface, making it a test bed for schema, ordering, and cross-step dependency errors [ 3 ] . ToolSandbox adds stateful tool execution, implicit state dependencies, an on-policy user simulator, and dynamic intermediate/final milestone evaluation, making recovery after intermediate failure observable during the rollout [ 4 ] .
blocks.zh: 我们使用 BFCL v3 和 ToolSandbox 测试多步函数调用正确性和状态政策互动. BFCL v3在标准化接口下提供多回合函数调用假想,使其成为了"计划","命令","跨步依赖"错误的试验床[3]. ToolSandbox增加了状态性工具执行,隐含状态依赖,一个政策性用户模拟器,以及动态的中间/最后里程碑评价,使得中间失败后的恢复在推出过程中被观察到[4].

blocks.en: For each benchmark, we evaluate a stratified sample of N = 200 N=200 instances. The BFCL v3 subset is stratified uniformly over the four multi-turn categories used in this study: multi_turn_base , multi_turn_miss_func , multi_turn_miss_param , and multi_turn_long_context , with 50 50 tasks from each. The ToolSandbox subset contains 200 200 supported open-source scenario templates selected by a deterministic greedy multi-label stratifier over scenario-category labels. Sampling is performed once per dataset, and the same task IDs are reused for every model and method, so all method comparisons are paired at the task level. The BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox grid comprises 200 × 2 × 3 × 4 = 4,800 200\times 2\times 3\times 4=4{,}800 evaluated rollouts across two datasets, three models, and four agent variants. We report 95% task-level confidence intervals. Marginal-interval overlap does not establish paired significance, and we do not infer paired effects from it. For each rollout, we log whether each predicted call is executable, the first failing step, its primary error label, and whether the episode later reaches benchmark-defined task success. blocks.en: We compare a nested intervention ladder with four variants: 1. ReAct : interleaved reasoning and acting without explicit plan validation [ 2 ] . 2. Prompt Planning : a planner-first variant in which a plan is generated but not enforced during execution. 3. Plan-Conditioned ReAct : the generated plan is provided as an explicit control signal during execution. 4. Dual-Loop : the same plan-conditioned executor augmented with pre-execution verification. Within each LLM condition, executor calls share the same model setting, tool specification format, decoding strategy, and benchmark horizon cap. Planner and verifier calls occur before execution and are counted as method cost rather than tool actions in T i T_{i} . Additional provider-specific decoding and rollout settings are reported in Appendix E . We report three LLM conditions: GPT-5.4 ( reasoning.effort=high ), GPT-4.1, and Llama-4-Maverick-Instruct.

blocks.en: 4 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 4 结论

blocks.en: Reliable tool use is not only a question of whether an agent eventually succeeds, but whether its trajectory remains executable as it unfolds. This paper introduced prefix executability as an evaluation protocol for tool-using agents, formalizing PEC, FED, TER, AUC-PEC, and RR for variable-horizon rollouts. Across the three-benchmark audit, prefix reliability and terminal outcome provide complementary information. Validation improves prefix reliability on BFCL-v3 and ToolSandbox, while the Airline/Retail transfer audit and paired sensitivity study show that this benefit is environment-dependent. Exact identities explain how high final success can coexist with frequent prefix failure, and cost measurements expose the operational price of validation. Evaluations should therefore report uninterrupted executability, recovery, terminal success, and agent-side cost together.
blocks.zh: 可靠工具的使用不仅是一个物剂是否最终成功的问题,而且其轨迹是否随着其展开仍然可以被执行. 本文引入了前缀可执行性作为工具使用剂的评价协议,将PEC,FED,TER,AUC-PEC正式化,RR用于可变范围推出. 通过三个基准审计,前缀可靠性和终端结果提供了补充信息。 验证在BFCL-v3和TolleSandbox上提高了前缀的可靠性,而Airline/Retail transfer审计和配对敏感性研究表明,这种好处是环境上的依赖. 准确的身份解释最终的高成功率如何能与频繁的前缀故障并存,成本测量暴露了验证的操作价格. 因此,评价应报告不间断的可执行性、恢复、最终成功以及代理方费用。

blocks.en:
Although we report PEC, FED, TER, AUC-PEC, and RR as retrospective evaluation
metrics over completed rollouts, the underlying executable-prefix predicate is
prefix-local. When available during execution, it can be checked after each
candidate tool action to support runtime monitoring, repair, replanning, or
human escalation before invalid state is propagated. Aggregated over rollouts,
the same signals can guide offline choices such as prompt design, validation
budgets, and agent selection. These uses remain complementary to the paper’s
evaluation focus: prefix executability exposes whether and where a trajectory
becomes invalid, but it does not by itself certify semantic correctness, safety,
privacy, or fairness. Developing closed-loop agents and deployment policies that
optimize against these signals is an important direction for future work.

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: The study is an audit rather than a complete leaderboard evaluation: BFCL-v3 and ToolSandbox each contribute 200 sampled tasks, ToolSandbox is restricted to supported local-tool scenarios, and τ 3 \tau^{3} coverage is complete only for the Airline/Retail base splits. Task-level intervals do not measure within-task repeated-seed variation. The main-grid tables provide marginal intervals; paired intervals are reported for the separate verifier-sensitivity study. Fixed-cohort PEC reflects both reaching a depth and retaining validity, so its decline is not an error-only statistic.
blocks.zh: 这项研究是审计而不是完整的领导板评价:BFCL-v3和TolleSandbox各自贡献了200个被采样的任务,TolleSandbox仅限于支持的本地工具方案,而&tau^{3}的覆盖范围仅针对航空公司/零售基地拆分而完成. 任务级别间隔不测量任务内重复种子的变异. 主网格表提供边距;对接间隔报告用于单独的核查器-敏感性研究. 固定曲线的PEC既能达到深度,又能保持有效性,因此其衰减并非只计算出错误的统计数据.

blocks.en: Executability assumes explicit schemas, preconditions, and benchmark-accessible state. Partially observed web or GUI environments may require state estimation or learned preconditions, and executability does not certify semantic correctness. We did not evaluate a matched schema-constrained-decoding baseline, so the reported rankings are not established under such constraints. These constraints can prevent malformed arguments, while prefix checking additionally covers object existence, provenance, state preconditions, and transition acceptance.
blocks.zh: 可执行性假定有明确的计划、先决条件和基准无障碍状态。 部分观测到的网络或图形用户界面环境可能需要状态估计或学到的先决条件,可执行性不能证明语义正确. 我们没有评估一个相匹配的、受约束的、解码基线,因此所报告的排名不是在这种限制下确定的。 这些限制可以防止参数不正确,而前缀检查则会额外涵盖对象的存在,出处,状态先决条件,以及过渡接受等.

blocks.en: The intervention combines validation/revision with extra inference. The sensitivity study varies verifier capacity and budget, but its acceptance wrapper changes executor guidance; it does not fully separate validation logic from compute or context effects. Per-method cost telemetry is available for the τ 3 \tau^{3} audit, whereas the BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox grid has aggregate runtime only. Broader claims require additional domains, repeated runs, and matched constrained-decoding and repair controls.

blocks.en:
Prefix-level executability can improve oversight of tool-using agents by
identifying invalid API calls, unresolved dependencies, and state-precondition
violations before they are obscured by final-success scores. This is most useful
in workflows where tool calls modify persistent state, consume resources,
trigger external actions, or require human escalation. The same diagnostics may
also make autonomous tool use easier to deploy in settings with privacy,
security, fairness, or service-access risks. Moreover, an executable trajectory
can still be unsafe, biased, privacy-violating, or misaligned with user intent.
Prefix executability should therefore be treated as one reliability signal and
combined with domain-specific safety policies, privacy controls, security
review, and human oversight in consequential applications.

blocks.en: Table A.1 compares the evaluation units and signals of related protocols. Prefix executability measures whether the observed action sequence satisfies the benchmark’s schemas, state preconditions, and data dependencies. Alternative action sequences receive full executability credit whenever these conditions hold, regardless of agreement with a reference trajectory. Prefix metrics therefore complement evaluations of task outcomes, intermediate milestones, reference-trajectory agreement, and semantic process quality.

blocks.en: The verifier is designed to reject candidate plans that contain predictable sources of non-executable prefixes before any environment action is taken. It applies the following local checklist, aligned with the first-failure taxonomy in Section 2.4 : 1. Tool and schema validity. Each planned operation must refer to an available tool in 𝒰 \mathcal{U} , include required arguments, avoid unsupported arguments, and satisfy declared type or formatting constraints. 2. Dependency resolution. Values referenced by a planned step must be available from the prompt, the initial state summary, or an earlier planned step. The verifier rejects forward references, stale bindings, and type-incompatible reuse. 3. Information availability. Required user information or lookup results must either be present, requested before use, or represented as a dependency on an earlier planned step. This check catches plans that use information before collecting it. 4. Explicit preconditions. If a tool requires prior authorization, a preceding state update, or a specific object to exist before use, the plan must satisfy that prerequisite before the tool is called. 5. State consistency. Planned state mutations must be compatible with benchmark-visible state and with state changes induced by earlier planned steps. Examples include rejecting updates to absent objects or operations that consume unavailable resources. The checklist is intentionally local. It is not a proof of global optimality, and it does not replace benchmark replay after execution. The benchmark-side evaluator remains the authority for FED, TER, final success, and RR.

blocks.en: If the verifier rejects a candidate plan, its feedback identifies the earliest detected failing step, the failed check, and the information needed for repair when that information is available from x x , 𝒰 \mathcal{U} , or s 0 s_{0} . The planner then proposes a revised candidate before any environment-facing action is emitted. In the BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox experiments, the validation loop is capped at K val = 5 K_{\mathrm{val}}=5 candidate plans. If no candidate is accepted within this cap, the validation stage returns a failure flag and the executor receives no accepted plan as a strong constraint. The rollout is not discarded; any environment actions subsequently emitted by the executor are scored in the same way as all other rollouts. Cap exhaustion is therefore method-side behavior, not a prefix failure.

blocks.en: Our experiments evaluate agent rollouts rather than train or fine-tune models. All LLM inference was performed through hosted model APIs; the local machine only orchestrated benchmark execution, tool-state updates, trajectory logging, and metric computation. Model inference was served by provider-managed accelerator infrastructure behind API endpoints, so per-request GPU type, GPU count, and accelerator occupancy were not exposed to us. We therefore report local orchestration compute separately from hosted inference compute. The BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox grid contains 200 × 2 × 3 × 4 = 4,800 200\times 2\times 3\times 4=4{,}800 rollouts across two datasets, three models, and four agent variants. A CPU-only local worker is sufficient for the evaluation harness; the BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox runs used a Linux worker with 16 vCPUs and 64 GB RAM, with no local GPU allocated. Wall-clock time was dominated by remote model latency and API rate limits rather than local computation; using 16 asynchronous API-request workers, the 4,800-rollout BFCL-v3/ToolSandbox grid completed in approximately 72 hours. Offline computation of PEC, FED, TER, AUC-PEC, RR, and bootstrap confidence intervals for this grid completed in under 1 hour on the same machine.
